title: Gift Wrap Roll

drivers.name: Price increase (3.4%)
drivers.evidence: Recent sales at same price (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) show no lift; median x1.88 vs baseline, but one spike. Price increase likely dampens demand; historical promotions show no sustained lift at higher prices.

drivers.name: Heatwave (38°C)
drivers.evidence: No data on weather impact, but heatwaves reduce foot traffic; plausible demand reduction, especially for non-essential seasonal items.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 3.2. No events or promotions in target week. Price increased 3.4% to $5.72, which is above regular price ($5.53). Past promotions show weak average lift (x1.15, noise-adjusted x1.0), with post-promo dips (x0.84, noise-adjusted x1.0). Recent sales at $5.72 show no uplift: 2026-09-28 (1 unit, x0.31), 2026-10-05 (6 units, x1.88). Heatwave (38°C) may reduce shopping, but no evidence of weather impact on sales. No seasonal ramp in recent weeks. Classical model suggests no effect. Evidence is thin and inconsistent. Adjust downward slightly for price increase and heatwave.

brief:
PRODUCT: Gift Wrap Roll | category Seasonal | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 (4 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 5.72 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.53)
  planner notes: Heatwave forecast: 38°C all week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 3.2 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 10.4 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 8.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-95% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
